statusDetail: All 58 atomic checks received conclusive outcomes. Representative product and cart failures are recorded as site issues, not omitted work.

page.notes: The requested URL first serves an international selector. The US experience was audited via ?intl=nosplash. Coverage includes the selector, home, listing, search, product attempt, cart and sign-in. Checkout/payment submission, authenticated account management and store-pickup completion were not covered to avoid transactions or requiring credentials.

paths.description: International country and language selector, the default response for the requested URL.
US commerce homepage and global navigation, representing the marketing entry template.
Top Deals listing, representing a promoted category/listing template.
Laptop search results, representing product discovery, filtering and sponsored results.
Representative product detail reached from the shopping journey; direct navigation repeatedly returned ERR_HTTP2_PROTOCOL_ERROR.
Cart state, representing checkout entry and empty/loading recovery.
Sign-in form, representing account/authentication, autocomplete, passkey and validation behavior.

findings.summary: The storefront does not provide a user-preference-driven dark theme.
findings.evidence: The prefers-color-scheme: dark screenshot retains the same white page surfaces as the default capture, and the computed page color-scheme is normal.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and retint surfaces, text, controls and imagery inside prefers-color-scheme or with light-dark().

findings.summary: Animations continue when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion probe found six running animations with 3000 ms duration and infinite iterations while prefers-reduced-motion: reduce matched.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a reduced-motion query to stop auto-advancing and non-essential looping animation while retaining essential state feedback.

findings.summary: No high-contrast or forced-colors adaptation was found.
findings.evidence: The loaded CSS probe found no prefers-contrast or forced-colors rule, while controls depend heavily on blue/white styling.
findings.suggestedFix: Add forced-colors and prefers-contrast treatment that preserves control boundaries, focus and text visibility.

findings.summary: The large two-row navigation chrome does not respond to scroll state.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots show a fixed-height two-row header, and CSS inspection found no scroll-state(scrolled) query or progress treatment.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a scroll-state container query or a lightweight sticky-header state to reduce chrome after scrolling without obscuring context.

findings.summary: Global menus use custom body-locking behavior rather than semantic overlay primitives.
findings.evidence: Opening Shop sets body overflow:hidden, while the DOM probe found zero popover, dialog, details, or role=dialog elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement transient menus with popover and declarative light-dismiss, preserving keyboard focus and Escape behavior.

findings.summary: Core commerce pages break at a 360 px viewport.
findings.evidence: The mobile layout primitive measured scrollWidth 1069 px against clientWidth 360 px, 709 px horizontal overflow; screenshots show clipped headers, clipped cards and large blank regions.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix viewport/device-class detection and use intrinsic responsive layouts so innerWidth and content width remain 360 px without horizontal scrolling.

findings.summary: Several navigation targets are too short and one control loses focus indication.
findings.evidence: The focus probe measured multiple navigation links at 16 px high and the international selector CSS explicitly sets .language-menu button:focus { outline: 0 }.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide at least 44 CSS px touch targets and a clearly visible :focus-visible style without suppressing the default outline unless replaced.

findings.summary: The representative browse-to-cart flow does not complete reliably.
findings.evidence: Search rendered results, but direct product navigation returned ERR_HTTP2_PROTOCOL_ERROR on desktop and mobile; cart captures remained an empty shell after seven seconds.
findings.suggestedFix: Make product and cart routes reliably render, preserve the selected product across navigation, and provide an actionable failure state when backend delivery fails.

findings.summary: Blank product/cart states offer no status or recovery.
findings.evidence: The failed product capture shows a browser protocol error and the cart capture shows only global chrome with a blank content region, no loading, empty, retry, or back-to-shopping state.
findings.suggestedFix: Render bounded loading skeletons, explicit error/empty copy, Retry and Continue shopping actions, and preserve focus/context.

findings.summary: Loading performance is far outside the good Core Web Vitals range.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 8.9 s, TBT 3,150 ms and Speed Index 13.1 s (performance 31); the independent trace measured FCP/LCP 9.38 s.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP resource, reduce startup JavaScript, and schedule non-critical work after the primary content is usable.

findings.summary: The mobile layout shifts materially during load.
findings.evidence: The mobile layout observer recorded CLS 0.186 with a largest individual shift of 0.115, above the good threshold.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve stable space for late content, use explicit dimensions/aspect-ratio, and avoid injecting banners above existing content.

findings.summary: Heavy scripting blocks the main thread.
findings.evidence: The trace found seven long tasks, a 659 ms longest task and 1,323 ms TBT; Lighthouse measured 3,150 ms TBT, 7.2 s JS execution and 9.9 s main-thread work.
findings.suggestedFix: Break long tasks, defer low-value widgets and analytics, and load route-specific code only when needed.

findings.summary: Resource delivery contains a large render-blocking and weak-cache burden.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 275 requests and 6.66 MB transferred, including ten parser-inserted VeryHigh-priority stylesheets; Lighthouse estimates 900 ms render-blocking and 844 KiB cache savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate/inline critical CSS, defer non-critical styles, improve immutable cache lifetimes and shorten dependency chains.

findings.summary: The page ships several megabytes of unnecessary JavaScript.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 150 scripts transferring 6.06 MB, including a 1.06 MB chunk; Lighthouse estimates 3,156 KiB unused JavaScript and 54 KiB unused CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Code-split by visible feature, remove duplicate/legacy bundles, and lazy-load chat, ads and account widgets after intent.

findings.summary: Some links and ARIA attributes are not accessible.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility scored 84 and failed link-name and aria-allowed-attr; the image audit also reported 15 images without alt attributes.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every actionable link an accessible name, remove invalid ARIA attributes, and use empty alt only for confirmed decorative images.

findings.summary: Heading/focus structure is not consistently logical.
findings.evidence: The US homepage rendered no h1, Lighthouse flagged positive tabindex, and the international language buttons explicitly suppress their focus outline.
findings.suggestedFix: Add one descriptive h1, keep DOM/tab order natural, remove positive tabindex and style :focus-visible clearly.

findings.summary: The page restricts zoom and fails narrow reflow.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed meta-viewport because user scaling is disabled or maximum-scale is below 5; mobile evidence shows 709 px overflow and 16 px-high links.
findings.suggestedFix: Allow user scaling, remove restrictive viewport directives, fix reflow and enlarge compact navigation targets.

findings.summary: The page logs browser console errors.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed errors-in-console during the audited load.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve first-party exceptions and failed requests, and gate optional integrations so they fail silently with telemetry rather than console errors.

findings.summary: Document assets include sizing and deprecated-platform defects.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found unsized images and two deprecated API warnings; the image audit found 17 images without responsive sources and two oversized images.
findings.suggestedFix: Add intrinsic dimensions and srcset/sizes, migrate deprecated APIs, and keep the valid doctype/UTF-8 foundation.

findings.summary: Browser-platform hygiene is weak.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found three BFCache failure reasons, missing source maps for large first-party JS, inspector issues, deprecated APIs and console errors.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove avoidable BFCache blockers, publish production source maps securely, and clear DevTools deprecation/Issues warnings.

findings.summary: Robots and link-text signals are defective.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse SEO scored 85, reported an invalid robots.txt and two links without descriptive text.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a syntactically valid robots.txt and replace empty/generic anchor text with descriptive accessible names.

findings.summary: Indexing signals are inconsistent.
findings.evidence: The canonical URL is present, but Lighthouse reports invalid robots.txt; the raw crawler fetch also failed, preventing reliable non-JS retrieval in this run.
findings.suggestedFix: Make robots.txt reliably retrievable and valid, keep sitemap/robots/canonical policies aligned, and monitor crawler response status.

findings.summary: The commerce homepage lacks structured and share-preview metadata.
findings.evidence: The holistic DOM probe found zero JSON-LD blocks and no og:title on a public retail homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Organization/WebSite/Product JSON-LD where applicable and complete Open Graph/Twitter preview metadata.

findings.summary: Core transport defenses and cookie flags are missing.
findings.evidence: The HTTPS document lacked CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame protection, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy; 26 cookies were flagged insecure and many used SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy HSTS, a nonce/hash-based CSP, nosniff and appropriate frame/referrer/permissions policy; set Secure and the narrowest SameSite/HttpOnly cookie attributes.

findings.summary: Tracking and third-party activity are disproportionate.
findings.evidence: The tracker probe found 24 third-party origins and eight known advertising trackers; HAR recorded 78 third-party requests transferring 1.26 MB.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove low-value trackers, delay consent-dependent tags, batch analytics, and document the purpose/retention of remaining vendors.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are absent.
findings.evidence: Header inspection found no HSTS, clickjacking protection, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy or CSP/frame-ancestors.
findings.suggestedFix: Add defense-in-depth response policies and test them in report-only mode before enforcement.

findings.summary: Core storefront content is not reliably available to a non-JavaScript crawler.
findings.evidence: The discoverability run produced a blank crawler screenshot and 0% raw-content coverage while the rendered view contained 170 content tokens; the raw fetch failed.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render core headings, offers, links and product content, with JavaScript enhancing rather than supplying the only usable experience.

findings.summary: Runtime route failures degrade to blank or browser-error states.
findings.evidence: Product navigation produced ERR_HTTP2_PROTOCOL_ERROR and the cart rendered global chrome over an empty content region with no in-page fallback.
findings.suggestedFix: Use route-level error boundaries, timeouts and fallback HTML, and make optional async dependencies conditional.

findings.summary: Network/HTTP failures do not provide actionable recovery.
findings.evidence: Repeated product and cart captures exposed a browser protocol error or blank shell without Retry, Continue shopping, status copy or preserved context.
findings.suggestedFix: Handle document/API failure with explicit error states, retry/back actions and stale-but-useful content where safe.

findings.summary: The commercial journey cannot reliably reach a usable cart state.
findings.evidence: Search results are visible but the product route failed and cart body remained blank; pricing/commitment and checkout controls therefore could not be reviewed or reversed in the primary path.
findings.suggestedFix: Restore reliable product/cart rendering and keep price, fulfillment, commitment and reversal controls visible at each step.

findings.summary: Image delivery is not consistently responsive or right-sized.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 17 of 25 images without srcset, two oversized assets and one below-fold image loaded eagerly; Lighthouse estimates 165 KiB image savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP responsive variants with srcset/sizes, retain dimensions and lazy-load non-critical imagery.

findings.summary: The homepage performs substantial non-essential work before usefulness.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 275 requests, 150 scripts and 6.66 MB; trace LCP was 9.38 s with 1.32 s TBT, while many analytics/chat endpoints remained active.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove redundant fetches, deprioritize background work and initialize chat/ads/analytics only after user intent or idle.

findings.summary: Third-party scripts exceed a proportionate homepage budget.
findings.evidence: Third parties made 78 requests and transferred 1.26 MB; known advertising trackers included DoubleClick, Google Ads and Tag Manager.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget, remove low-value vendors and defer remaining tags behind consent and interaction.

findings.summary: A high-value commerce site exposes weak agent-facing structure.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse agentic-browsing scored 33 and failed accessibility-tree and llms.txt recommendations; discoverability produced a blank crawler view.
findings.suggestedFix: First make products/actions server-visible and accessibility-tree-correct, then expose bounded, confirmable commerce actions through agentic forms/WebMCP where appropriate.

findings.summary: Repeated menu interaction showed material retained-heap growth.
findings.evidence: Baseline-to-post heap snapshots after ten Shop open/Escape cycles grew from 135.4 MB/2,127,297 nodes to 152.5 MB/2,333,939 nodes (12.6% bytes, 9.7% nodes). Separate page loads can add noise, so confidence is medium.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile retained paths across baseline/target/final snapshots and clean up menu closures, observers and listeners on close.

findings.summary: The homepage memory footprint is disproportionate.
findings.evidence: The baseline heap snapshot contained 2,127,297 heap nodes and 135.4 MB self size; the independent performance probe reported about 118.6 MB used JS heap for 858 DOM elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce startup bundles and retained application state, lazy-initialize widgets and establish a heap budget for the homepage.

findings.summary: Heap-node growth after repeated menu cycles warrants detached-node/listener investigation.
findings.evidence: Ten open/close cycles were followed by 206,642 additional heap nodes and 17.1 MB additional self size. Constructor-level detached-node data and listener enumeration were unavailable, so confidence is low.
findings.suggestedFix: Use DevTools retained-path analysis to distinguish caches from detached DOM; ensure menu listeners, observers and timers are removed on close.

Cut startup JavaScript, requests and main-thread work to meet Core Web Vitals
Deploy security headers and strict cookie attributes
Reduce tracking and enforce a third-party resource budget
Repair names, structure, focus and target sizing
Server-render crawlable core content and metadata
Honor dark, reduced-motion and high-contrast preferences
Investigate retained heap growth across repeated menu interactions
Adopt semantic popover/menu behavior and scroll-aware chrome
Clear console, BFCache, source-map and deprecated API defects
